newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia selling another power generation asset.
newsitem.headline: Colombia selling another power generation asset.

text.p: The Colombian government will sell off its 57 percent stake in Empresas de Energia del Pacifico SA (EPSA), the state-run power company serving Cali and southwest Valle del Cauca province, on April 18, a business consultant handling the privatization said Tuesday.

The consultant, Juan Fernando Bonilla, told Reuters the government had set a base price of $500 million for its share in the company, which consists of four hydroelectric plants and one thermoelectric facility with a combined power generating capacity of at least 820 megawatts.

According to Bonilla, a dozen companies from the United States, Canada, Britain, Spain, Chile and Venezuela have expressed interest in the government stake in EPSA and are likely to participate in the bidding process beginning April 11.
The winning bidder will be announced on April 18, he said.
The government received nearly $1.2 billion in the final quarter of 1996 through the successful sales of two hydroelectric plants and two thermoelectric plans.
The sales allowed foreign operators to enter the country's power generation sector for the first time.
